newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LDP panel head says to mull land tax.
newsitem.headline: Japan LDP panel head says to mull land tax.

text.p: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) is to discuss how to treat a tax on land holdings for the year starting in April 1998, said Yoshiro Hayashi, chairman of the LDP's tax research council.

Many members of Japan's parliament favour scrapping the land holding tax, which was introduced in 1992 to curb the late 1980s economic bubble of inflated land prices, he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
But he said the panel must consider the land holding tax, which now stands at 1.5 percent, in the context of the overall land taxation system.
He also said it must consider whether land prices, which have fallen rapidly since the economic bubble burst, have reached an appropriate level.
"We must consider whether scrapping the land holding tax might result in helping the reemergence of land speculation, as scrapping it could contribute to lowering land prices," he said.

Hayashi also said the LDP council would discuss whether and how Japan should introduce a consolidated tax system for group companies, which would be a major factor for banks in deciding whether to set up holding companies -- firms which control one or more other firms but do not themselves engage in a specific business.

He said a decision on the issue would be made after taking account of the progress of domestic firms in shifting their accounting standards towards a consolidated system from the current system focusing on business results of the parent company.

Parliament passed a bill to lift a decades-old ban on holding companies last month. The measure is expected to take effect in December. The Finance Ministry is expected to submit another bill legalising financial holding companies in a special session of parliament this autumn.
As for scrapping the securities transaction tax, Hayashi said the council has not made a final decision on the issue.

He said that while the council had received a proposal to scrap the securities transaction tax from another LDP council, Japan must first discuss whether it would rely on the capital gains tax to offset the scrapping of the securities transaction tax in the context of overall tax revenue.

Last month, Japan's Securities and Exchange Council, an advisory panel to the Finance Minister, proposed deregulation of Japan's securities markets, in which it urged authorities to consider abolishing securities transaction taxes to improve the efficiency of Japan's securities markets.
"It is important to seek the revitalisation of Japan's stock market," he said.
